narrative.title: The Dispatch Ledger Decoder
narrative.scenario: A logistics hub receives machine-generated dispatch codes written operator-first (`- A B` meaning A minus B) and human auditors need them back in ordinary form. Because an operator-first code always names the operation before listing its two operands, the decoder scans backwards, keeping partially built operand groups on a shelf, and joins the top two groups whenever an operator appears.
narrative.inputFormat: A string expression in valid prefix form with single alphanumeric operands.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the fully parenthesized infix expression as a string.
constraints: Operands are single letters or digits
The expression is guaranteed to be a valid prefix expression

testCases.explanation: Scanning backwards, each operator wraps the two groups already on the shelf, rebuilding the parenthesized tree.
The minimal case: one operator, two operands, one pair of parentheses.

Level 2: Scan right-to-left so operands are already waiting when their operator arrives.
